To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) heat transfer through porous cable insulation into He-II bath is improved by a factor up to 2.5, with respect to standard cable insulation, and (2) heat transfer is not affected by a localized heat deposition in the coil, as long as a sufficient number of cables is involved.

(i) the heat transfer through the enhanced insulation scheme is larger than through the standard insulation; (ii) this difference is more pronounced at higher applied pressure; (iii) the heat transfer is larger in case of a distributed heat deposition, compared to the localized heat deposition.
the Enhanced Insulation Scheme is able to provide a major improvement in heat transfer, up to high levels of compressive stress, compared to the standard cable insulation used in the LHC magnets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an insulation scheme that can be used in future high-field accelerator magnets, where heat transfer to the helium bath is critical.
the development of a new cable insulation scheme for the superconducting magnet coils of the next generation of particle colliders.
the development of a new insulation scheme for the superconducting magnets of the LHC luminosity upgrade, featuring an improved heat transfer into He-II bath.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enhanced insulation scheme is an excellent candidate for future magnets, in particular for the LHC luminosity upgrade.
the enhanced cable insulation scheme is promising for the LHC luminosity upgrade and future high field magnets.
the enhanced insulation scheme, with the present design of cable insulation, is not suitable for the application in the LHC luminosity upgrade.

, at least in the case of low compressive stress (as expected for the LHC luminosity upgrade magnets), the enhanced insulation scheme could be a promising alternative to the existing insulation scheme.
the enhanced insulation is a viable alternative for the next generation of superconductive magnets.
